jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Dynamic Modelling, Simulation and Optimization of Power-to-X Processes
jobs.description:
At the Faculty of Engineering and Science, AAU Energy, a 24-month postdoctoral position in Dynamic Modelling, Simulation and Optimization of Power-to-X Processes is available from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The project is primarily rooted in process engineering while also addressing interactions between Power-to-X plants and the electrical grid.

Your work tasks
You will develop and apply dynamic process models based on mass and energy balances, thermodynamics, reaction kinetics, and equipment behaviour to simulate integrated Power-to-X plants under changing operating conditions. The work will address renewable fuel production, particularly green methanol and sustainable aviation fuels through methanol-based and Fischer–Tropsch pathways. The work will focus on electrolysers, fuel-synthesis processes, energy storage, heat integration, and interactions with the electrical grid.

You will combine process simulation with operational optimization, process control, techno-economic assessment, and model validation to investigate flexible operation under varying renewable electricity generation and energy prices.

You will collaborate with academic and industrial partners, publish scientific results, contribute to project meetings and deliverables, and present findings at conferences and workshops. The position may also include limited teaching and supervision of bachelor’s and master’s students.

Your competencies
You hold a PhD in chemical engineering, process engineering, or a closely related field, completed by the application deadline. You have documented research experience in process modelling and simulation, preferably including dynamic modelling of chemical or energy processes.

Hands-on experience with Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS, or Aspen Dynamics will be considered a strong advantage. Experience with gPROMS, Modelica, or comparable process-simulation tools is also relevant. Strong skills in MATLAB, Python, or a similar computational environment are expected.

Experience with Power-to-X, renewable fuels, optimization, process control, model validation, techno-economic assessment, or grid-integrated energy systems will strengthen your profile.

You will work closely with industrial and international partners. Therefore, the ability to translate research into practical solutions and communicate effectively across disciplines is essential. We value candidates who are proactive, structured, collaborative, and motivated to publish high-quality research and contribute actively to project activities.

Who we are
You will join the Fluid & Process research group at AAU Energy, Campus Esbjerg, where you will become part of an international and interdisciplinary research environment combining process, chemical, energy and electrical engineering. The group works with modelling, simulation, control, optimization and experimental validation of fluid and energy systems, with applications including Power-to-X, carbon capture and utilization, green fuels and sector coupling. The working culture is collaborative and informal, with close interaction among academic staff, postdoctoral researchers, PhD fellows and students. We share an ambition to contribute to the green transition through research with practical relevance. We offer laboratory and workshop facilities, and a collaborative environment that supports innovation, knowledge sharing, and professional development.

Learn more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

Qualification requirements 
Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

How to apply  
Your application must include the following: 

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position 
• Curriculum Vitae (CV) 
• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma) 
• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of five publications. You must submit a co-author statement, see template for co-author statement 
• Documentation of teaching qualifications if relevant.
• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc. 
• Additional qualifications in relation to the position 
• References/recommendations 
You can read more about the requirements for your application here.    

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.  

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. 

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society. 

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment. 

Do you have any questions? 
If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.     

Further information 
Read more about our recruitment process here   

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.  

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. 

Salary and terms of employment  
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Postdoc”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world
Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

jobs.occupation: Two-year postdoc in greenhouse gas emissions and nutrient retention in agricultural waters
jobs.description:
The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University invites applications for a two-year postdoc position in the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management in Aarhus, starting 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The position combines research on nitrous oxide emissions from agricultural nitrogen losses to surface waters with a synthesis of greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in mitigation measures for agricultural drainage water.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a two-year position from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description

We are seeking a motivated postdoc to work on two closely linked research activities throughout the position.

Nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions from nitrogen that leaches from agricultural fields to streams, lakes and other water bodies are estimated to make up around 5% of the Danish agricultural sector’s greenhouse gas emissions, but this estimate is highly uncertain. The Aqua-N2O project, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF), aims to identify the drivers of these aquatic N2O emissions using high-frequency in-situ sensor monitoring, providing the scientific basis for modelling the emissions at regional scale and for evaluating mitigation strategies.

Drainage mitigation measures. Measures that intercept nutrients in agricultural drainage water before it reaches streams, such as surface flow and subsurface flow constructed wetlands, integrated buffer zones, saturated buffer zones and controlled drainage, are a key part of Danish water management. They can remove substantial amounts of nitrogen, but some may also release phosphorus and emit greenhouse gases such as N2O and methane. You will synthesise results on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention from Danish drainage mitigation measures to give an overall assessment of their environmental performance and trade-offs.

Your main tasks will be to:

• carry out fieldwork, including sensor deployment and water and gas sampling

• process and analyse high-frequency sensor data and monitoring data

• compile and synthesise existing data on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in drainage mitigation measures

• write scientific papers for international peer-reviewed journals

Your profile

The successful candidate must hold a PhD degree in biogeochemistry, aquatic ecology, environmental science, hydrology or a related field, and have a valid driving licence, as the position involves fieldwork in Danish agricultural landscapes.

It is an advantage if you have:

• experience with measurements of greenhouse gases (e.g. N2O, CH4) in aquatic systems or soils

• knowledge of nitrogen and phosphorus cycling in agricultural catchments, wetlands or constructed wetlands

• experience with analysis of large or high-frequency datasets, e.g. in R or Python

• a documented record of publishing in international peer-reviewed journals

We are looking for a candidate who can work independently as well as in a team, and who has good written and spoken English.

Who we are

The Department of Ecoscience is engaged in research programs and advisory work covering the major biological sub-disciplines. We conduct innovative, advanced research in the areas of aquatic biology and ecology, Arctic environments and ecosystems, biodiversity, conservation biology, and wildlife management. The Department currently employs approximately 300 academic and technical staff, as well as many PhD students.

The successful candidate will work in a supportive and internationally engaged scientific environment at the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management. The section’s research and advisory work covers nutrient dynamics and hydrology, mitigation measures to reduce nutrient losses to the aquatic environment, and wetlands and greenhouse gases. The section has developed and tested many of the mitigation measures used in Danish water management, including constructed wetlands for treating drainage water, and advises national and international authorities.

The department aims to be a supportive and encouraging workplace that offers interesting challenges, collaborative colleagues, and avenues for academic growth. The department actively facilitates a healthy integration of work and personal life and aspires to recruit and maintain highly skilled individuals who prioritise curiosity and trust.

What we offer

The department offers:

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment

• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators

• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research

• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities

• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment

The place of work is Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. Fieldwork will take place at sites in Denmark.

Contact information

For further information, please contact Senior Researcher Joachim Audet, joau@ecos.au.dk.

Deadline

Applications must be received no later than 1 December 2026.

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.

Formalities and salary range

Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: Technical Operations Manager, Technical Asset Performance DK
jobs.description:
Do you have solid technical know-how and a passion for contributing to the green transition? Then you might be our new Technical Operations Manager in Technical Asset Performance DK!

Who we are

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 countries around Europe and in the USA, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation's "Power Major". Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for an experienced Technical Operations Manager to join our dedicated Technical Asset Performance DK team. Based at our office in Hobro, you will be a central link between operations, projects and technical specialists.

Your role

You will play a key role in the performance, reliability and continuous optimization of our portfolio, taking ownership of complex technical topics and driving them from identification to resolution. You will work across Wind, BESS, PV and HV, with responsibilities ranging from daily operations to long-term optimization.

• End-to-end technical asset management, from infrastructure to component level

• Troubleshooting, root cause analysis and incident handling

• Planning and coordinating major maintenance activities and shutdowns

• Commissioning and integration of new parks and turbines

• Analyzing operational data and developing monitoring and performance platforms

• Collaboration with the surveillance team, service providers and contractors

• Technical reporting and sparring for internal and external stakeholders, including investor clarifications

Required competencies and skills

You have a solid technical background, preferably from renewable energy and asset management. You work in a structured, analytical way and balance technical excellence with an understanding of the commercial impact of your decisions.

• A technical education

• Experience within asset management

• Experience within several of Wind, BESS, PV and HV is an advantage

• A hands-on mindset and a strong technical toolbox

• Ability to work autonomously and drive tasks end-to-end

• Proficient English and flexibility to travel to sites a few times a year

• Driver's license (B); full GWO package is an advantage

What we offer

A dynamic role with a high degree of flexibility and variety, where priorities shift with operational needs, technical challenges and project timelines. You will report to Laurits H Østergaard, Manager, Technical Asset Performance DK, and join a dedicated team in our Hobro office, working closely with Asset Management colleagues in and outside Denmark.

• Hands-on ownership of technical topics across Wind, BESS, PV and HV

• Variety between daily operations, projects and deep technical investigations

• A culture where you can speak up, and support for your professional development

Renewable energy is our future. And so are our people!

At Eurowind Energy we do our best to create a culture where everyone is valued and feels at home. You will notice this in your everyday work life, where you have the freedom to speak up and where your voice means something to us. We know that when you grow, we grow. Therefore, we strive to support you in what you believe is right and in your personal and professional development. We offer you an exciting job in an energetic and international environment. And we promise you: the wind is never standing still.

Developing, operating and managing wind and solar parks is not just pure business for us. It is a way to view the world. And with this worldview comes a genuine ambition to be one of the leading developers in Europe. Because creating a future run entirely on green energy matters to us.

We manage our own portfolio of projects and at the same time, we perform technical and financial management of projects. We have throughout many years experienced sustained economic growth in the number of developed projects and companies in management. And we continue to expect this. Simply because it is in our nature to keep developing – projects, companies and our people.

Read more about Eurowind Energy A/S on our website or LinkedIn

Did we capture your attention?

Great! If you see yourself in this role, do not hesitate to apply for the position. Please use the link below. As we continuously review incoming applications, please send us your CV as soon as possible.

Should you have any questions before applying, please feel free to contact Laurits H Østergaard, Manager, Technical Asset Performance DK, at lauo@ewe.dk.

Application deadline:

As soon as possible

jobs.occupation: Student Worker | Talent Acquisition
jobs.description:
At KMD, we build digital solutions used by millions of people around the world. These solutions are the digital foundations of our most important institutions, from governments and public services to financial industries and private companies. Our mission is to ensure that they are reliable, accessible, and efficient.

We believe that the future is what you make it. So a career at KMD is a career with purpose and freedom. One where you’ll have a direct hand in improving the lives of people, while being empowered with the resources and autonomy to shape the course of your own professional journey.

Are you interested in how recruitment and HR-processes play out in a large Danish IT-company? Then you might be our new student Worker in the Talent Acquisition team in KMD!

We are expanding KMD’s Talent Acquisition team and are looking for a Student Worker to join us. The team is part of People, consisting of approximately 47 employees across Denmark and Poland. People supports KMD’s strategy and future direction, with attracting and selecting the right candidates playing a crucial role in achieving these goals.

About the job

The Talent Acquisition team consists of 7 people across Poland and Denmark. In Denmark, the team includes 1 Talent Acquisition Partner and 1 Student Worker. Together, we work towards the common goal of attracting and hiring the best candidates for KMD.

As a Student Worker, you will be part of the daily processes alongside the rest of the team and thus work with a broad spectrum of tasks related to recruitment. The tasks will consist of a mix of own responsibilities and ad-hoc support for the Talent Acquisition Partners and may include:

• Providing administrative support to the Talent Acquisition Partners

• Handling recruitment-related inquiries and managing communication via ServiceNow

• Conducting references

• Updating recruitment material in SharePoint

• Scheduling interviews

• Opportunity to participate in various projects depending on your interests and skills.

In addition to supporting the team with ad hoc recruitment tasks, you will work closely with another Student Worker to manage our student recruitment activities, including:

• Managing student recruitment processes end to end

• Working closely with Hiring Managers and leading recruitment kick-off meetings

• Providing feedback on cognitive assessments

• Handle contract creations.

This position is well suited for candidates considering a career in HR. You will be introduced to core HR and recruitment processes and gain insight into the strategy, goals, value chains and day-to-day operations in a large organization.

We offer an open, honest, and social office culture. As a KMD employee, you can expect a dynamic work environment with close collaboration across borders.

About you

• You are in your second or third year of a relevant bachelor’s and eager to learn about HR and recruitment

• You enjoy collaborating with various stakeholders and have a service-minded approach

• You are organized and detail-oriented

• You communicate fluently in both Danish and English

• You are comfortable using IT tools or are quick to learn new systems.

We work with SuccessFactors, ServiceNow, and Microsoft Office, and will provide thorough training on our tools and processes. We take pride in open communication and learning from each other.

Being a student in People and KMD

The working hours are approximately 15 hours per week. You will primarily work from our office in Ballerup, with the option to work from home. We offer flexibility during exam periods to support your studies.

As a Student Worker at KMD, you will have the opportunity to join our student network and participate in both social and professional events.

You will be supported by experienced colleagues in People and have ample opportunity to build a strong network across the organization through team activities, projects, and company-wide events.

Interested?

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. If you have any questions regarding the position, please feel free to contact Enas Karim at ekm@kmd.dk.

We look forward to receiving your application.

jobs.occupation: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Lead engineering at a profitable, funded proptech while the team is still small enough to shape.

• Want to set the technical direction for a growing team and still ship code yourself?

• How would you keep a small team shipping to production many times a day, with review and testing that catch problems before customers do, without every decision landing on your desk?

• Where would you draw the line between what an AI agent should suggest and what it can do on a property owner’s behalf?

Sounds like you? Then you might be our next CTO!

A property owner with a portfolio of buildings has a practical question: which repairs belong in next year’s budget, and which can wait? At Proprty.ai, our models estimate the condition and remaining life of building components and the energy and CO2 effect of improving them. Our software turns those estimates into maintenance plans, and our AI agent, Tily, helps owners analyze their portfolios and take action!

Our product went live in 2024 and is used by customers in Denmark, Norway and Germany. We reached profitability by the end of 2025 and raised DKK 21 million in April 2026, and we are not planning to stop there!

There is still so much we can do to make it even better, and you could help shape the future of building maintenance and how engineering is run at Proprty.ai.

Product: TypeScript, React, and Next.js on Vercel, with Supabase (PostgreSQL, row-level security, storage).**

Data and models: Python and PySpark on Databricks (Azure, EU), Python model services, and LLM features on Azure OpenAI. We also run a customer API and an MCP server.

What you get to shape

The team and the code.

You'll lead our product engineering team, work closely with our data engineers and our Chief Data Science Officer, and keep building core features yourself. You might coach a developer through a tricky problem in the morning and ship a feature yourself that afternoon. You'll own engineering hiring as the team grows, from deciding which roles we need to choosing the people you want on the team.

How we build and ship.

You’ll own the platform’s architecture and how we test and release. We release to production many times a day. Your job is to keep that pace while making every release reliable and secure. When an urgent customer request competes with longer-term platform work, you’ll make the call and explain what comes first and why.

Shape what Tily can do next.

Our data scientists build models for building condition, remaining life, cost, and energy across several European markets. Together with our Chief Data Science Officer, you'll get those models in front of customers, decide what Tily may do on an owner's behalf, and use feedback from property owners, Sales, and Customer Success to choose the next problems to solve.

Change how we use AI ourselves.

Change how we use AI ourselves. Our engineers build with Claude Code and Cursor, AI agents review every pull request in our CI/CD pipeline, and agents take on routine work end to end so the team can ship faster. We keep looking for new ways AI can raise our pace, and you'll lead that.

We talk a lot (in a good way). When a problem gets tricky, we pull up a chair and pair on it. We like having a laugh while we figure things out.

What you’ll bring?

You've been CTO or head of engineering at a startup or scale-up while the product, the team, and the rules were still taking shape, and you can show what changed because you were there. You know when to open a pull request yourself, when to let another engineer make the call, and which shortcut will come back to bite you two releases from now.

You bring curiosity about our industry, our customers' problems, and the business acumen to understand how our product delivers business value, so that you can help facilitate features that drive outcomes and make our users' lives easier.

We’re AI-first (the name’s a bit of a giveaway). If you’ve built an agent or shipped an AI feature, we’d love to hear what happened after the demo. What did customers trust it to do, and where did they want the controls back? You’ll get to make those calls with Tily and figure out where AI helps our own engineers ship better software.

The core of what we consider for a candidate

• You’ve led an engineering team, coached developers, and hired people to join it.

• You’re keen to build AI agents that customers can put to work and to explore where AI makes your own team more effective.

• You still build full-stack features with React, TypeScript, and SQL. You can take a feature from technical design through thoughtful user experience to release, and measure what happens when customers get their hands on it.

• Fluent in English

Experience we’d love to hear about

• Taking an engineering team from a startup to a scale-up phase, understanding how and when to mature processes as the team scales, and how that looks different in this new AI era.

• Shipping an AI agent or feature into production. We’re especially curious about what you changed after people started using it.

• How you’ve spoken with customers and industry experts to help ensure we’re on the forefront of solving the right problems in our platform

• Your perspective on the role of a CTO as a thought leader.

• Working with PostgreSQL or Next.js, or building products for real estate or proptech.

Where we work

We spend 4 days a week together in our office near Rådhuspladsen. You’ll need to be based in the Copenhagen area, as we can’t offer relocation or visa sponsorship for this role.

New to proptech? That’s fine. If you’ve led engineers and still enjoy being one, we’d love to hear from you.

Questions? Reach out to Casper Høgh at Csh@ing.dk, who helps us land the right human for the job

Our hiring process

• 
Intro call with Casper Høgh – We’ll talk about your background, what you want from your next CTO role, and any questions you have about proprty.ai.

•

jobs.description:
A postdoc position focusing on statistical genetic and the modelling of quantitative and disease resistance traits in commercial crops is available in March 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter at the Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG), Aarhus University.

The position

The postdoc will develop statistical models and methods in a new breeding program for cultivar mixtures primarily in wheat, supporting higher yield stability and disease resistance for sustainable wheat production.

Special focus will be on using genomic prediction for more efficient selection of new wheat lines and with special focus on prediction of the performance in cultivar mixtures specific combining ability between lines which raises interesting questions regarding experimental design and associated information of variation in the soil microbiome. This involves estimation of variance component models including microbiome and host relations to handle the genotype by environment interactions for traits recorded under different locations and environment conditions. Additionally, information of both genotyped and non-genotyped individuals need to be combined. Methods for evaluation and comparison of models should be developed and implemented in breeding schemes that involve traditional monoline information as well as phenotypic information from populations of mixtures. The postdoc is expected to pursue internationally recognized research in computational methods for genetic evaluation such as linear mixed models, hierarchical models with random effects. We in particular welcome applicants with interest in method development for large scale genetic evaluation using dense genomic information. The position is for 2 years of employment and there are possibilities for extension up to a maximum of 4 years if the candidate is considered qualified and sufficient funding is available. The position is related to collaborative projects together with commercial breeding companies with the goal of developing methods and models that can be implemented in commercial breeding programs. The future of climate action extends beyond reducing emissions
Atmospheric CO2 concentrations continue to rise despite global efforts to reduce emissions. Achieving climate neutrality will therefore require not only deep emission reductions but also large-scale carbon removal solutions. Direct Air Capture (DAC) is one of the few technologies capable of permanently removing CO2 directly from the atmosphere, but significant scientific and engineering challenges remain before DAC can be deployed at gigaton scale. Future DAC systems must be energy-efficient, economically viable, and designed around a fundamental understanding of how materials, processes, and system integration interact.

At Aalborg University, we are seeking ambitious PhD candidates who want to help develop the next generation of DAC technologies through advanced process modelling, experimental studies, and techno-economic evaluations.

The stipend is open for appointment from 1 January 2027 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

In the future, removing CO2 from the atmosphere will become an essential part of climate action.
Atmospheric CO2 is already changing the climate. Reducing emissions is essential, but it may not be enough. We must also learn how to remove carbon already present in the atmosphere. Future Direct Air Capture systems will not simply capture CO2:

They will integrate with renewable energy systems. They will operate flexibly and balance the energy systems. They will become scalable climate infrastructure.

What this PhD is really about
The stipends are designed to contribute to two ambitious research initiatives that aim to accelerate the development of Direct Air Capture technologies:

Development of process-aware methodologies for evaluating emerging DAC liquid and solid sorbents and technologies. Development of predictive frameworks linking sorbent properties to process-level DAC performance.

Together, these efforts seek to establish the scientific foundations required to move DAC development from empirical trial-and-error toward predictive, data-driven design and scale-up.

jobs.occupation: Academic employee at Land-CRAFT, Department of Agroecology, Aarhus University
jobs.description:
Would you like to help support research and development in a supportive and collaborative environment?
The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University is seeking a new employee for running lab-scale experiments with intact soil cores to assess the effect of different fertilizers and supplements, such as rock flour, on soil gaseous nitrogen losses and soil nitrogen leaching, with a starting date of 1st March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is available for a fixed term of 18 months.

The position is based on a 37-hour work week. Depending on the nature of the role and its responsibilities, periods of high workload may occur, during which overtime should be expected.

You will become part of Land-CRAFT, where you will work closely with researchers, technical and administrative colleagues, and, where relevant, students. The position is directly linked to two ongoing GUDP projects: RockFlour and Opti-BioN, and it offers an opportunity to contribute to the department’s core activities and daily operations within an active and engaging research environment.

Your tasks
• Designing and running soil core experiments
• Measuring the soil physical and chemical properties, calculating greenhouse gas fluxes, processing and interpreting data 
• Project management tasks, including communicating with the project partners and organizing meetings
• Preparing reports to funders and contributing to grant applications with data, plots, analyses and writing
Your profile

We expect that
• You have an MSc in Agricultural, Environmental, Soil Sciences, or similar
• You can demonstrate a minimum of two years' experience in designing and running soil experiments targeting greenhouse gas (GHG) balances and nitrogen (N) leaching.
• You have experience of measuring the soil properties and calculating greenhouse gas fluxe
• You have good English skills, and you thrive in an inclusive multi-cultural and diverse working environment
• You are motivated by working on projects, where the overall aim is to support the green transition in agriculture
• You are able to work on your own
Who we are
 At the Department of Agroecology, our main goal is to contribute to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. The department consists of nine research sections with around 350 highly skilled employees, of which approximately 50% are scientific staff. More information can be found here.

We believe in encouraging inclusion, acceptance, and understanding by employing staff who bring unique perspectives to our department.

What we offer
• A collaborative, international research environment that combines high academic standards with an informal and supportive atmosphere. We value accountability, curiosity, flexibility, and teamwork in everything we do.
• An inclusive and respectful workplace culture, where mutual trust, kindness, and professional dialogue are part of daily life. We encourage open communication and develop a cohesive sense of community across teams and disciplines.
• A flexible working environment that supports work-life balance and individual needs.
• An active institutional commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion – in recruitment, career development, and everyday interactions.
• An innovative and meaningful workplace where your work contributes to solving real-world challenges. No two days are alike, and we welcome creative thinking and new ideas.
• Support for international researchers and their families, including Relocation Service and an Expat Partner Programme
Living and working in Denmark
• Subsidised childcare and free education from primary school through university.
• Universal healthcare for you and your family as residents.
• Five weeks of paid holiday per year.
• Generous parental leave – up to 52 weeks shared between parents, with full or partial salary.
Place of Work
The place of work Ole Worms Alle 3, Department of Agroecology, Faculty of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University.

Contact
Applicants seeking further information can contact Professor Klaus Butterbach-Bahl (e-mail: klaus.butterbach-bahl@agro.au.dk)

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 24 November 2026. 

Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk
